title: Reduce autoscaler thrash by probe filtering and regional circuit-breaker implementation
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem statement:
Over the last two quarters we've observed repeated autoscaler thrash and unnecessary regional failovers tied to noisy liveness/readiness probe signals. Short-lived GC pauses, transient upstream errors, and occasionally overloaded inference workers cause probe flips that trigger scale-downs or regional fallback logic, which then causes capacity oscillation and SLO violations (p95/p99 spikes and error-budget burns).

Goals:
- Stabilize readiness/liveness signals so transient failures do not cause scaling churn.
- Introduce probe filtering and a regional circuit-breaker to prevent noisy nodes from triggering wide-area failovers.
- Implement graceful load-shedding policy for overload scenarios to protect p50/p95 latency for interactive workloads and preserve error budget.
- Provide observability and runbook updates so on-call can quickly diagnose probe-driven incidents.

Design summary (high level):
1) Probe filtering layer: implement a lightweight in-proxy filter that applies two mechanisms before surfaced probe flips reach the control plane: a) short-term hysteresis window (configurable 5–15s) where probe failures are counted with decay and require N failures within window to flip readiness; b) adaptive thresholding where probes for latency-sensitive routes use stricter health criteria while batch routes use relaxed checks.
2) Sticky readiness with backoff: when a replica transitions to NotReady due to heavy GC or transient DB error, mark it NotReady for a minimum sticky window (configurable) to avoid immediate re-add/remove cycles. The sticky period scales with recent probe-change rate.
3) Regional circuit-breaker: a policy at the topology layer that trips when a region's error budget burn or consecutive scale events exceed thresholds. While tripped, routing prefers local replicas and avoids cross-region failover unless manual override or canary clears the breaker. Circuit-breaker supports automatic recovery with exponential backoff and manual reset path.
4) Load-shedding policy: prioritized request classes (interactive > background) with soft reject and degrade paths. On overload, shed background/bulk requests first and return structured fallback responses for interactive calls (see structured-errors RFC).

Instrumentation and SLOs to monitor:
- probe_flip_rate (per replica, per region)
- probe_flip_duration_distribution
- scale_event_frequency and scale_delta_magnitude
- region_error_budget_burn_rate
- p50/p95/p99 request latency by route and region
- request_drop_rate and shed_count by class
- KV cache hit ratio and queue length metrics

Acceptance criteria (what "done" looks like):
- Reduce median probe_flip_rate by >=70% in canary region under typical workload replay.
- Reduce scale_event_frequency caused by probe flips by >=80% in canary.
- No increase in p99 latency outside a 5% tolerance for steady-state traffic.
- Circuit-breaker successfully trips/recovers in simulated region failure test with documented automatic and manual recovery steps.
- Dashboards, alerts, and runbook entries completed and reviewed by SRE and Support.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Week 1: Prototype probe-filtering logic in serving-side proxy, unit tests + local bench. (ENG-11813)
- Week 2: Add metrics and observability hooks; create dashboard skeleton and alert rules. (ENG-11814)
- Week 3: Implement regional circuit-breaker in topology orchestration layer; create canary gating. (ENG-11815)
- Week 4: Canary rollout to staging -> us-west-2 -> us-east-1; fault-injection tests (GC pauses, network partition, DB error bursts).
- Week 5: Analyze canary results, tune thresholds, prepare prod rollout and runbook handoff.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Increasing probe hysteresis can delay detection of true unhealthy replicas (longer MTTR). Mitigation: keep liveness probes for catastrophic failures unaffected and tune sticky windows conservatively; add emergency kill path for replicas that exceed resource limits.
- Circuit-breaker may prevent useful cross-region failovers for some customers; mitigation: expose per-customer override and canary to validate behavior for enterprise tenants.
- Load-shedding must preserve useful failure semantics; design will use structured error responses and client-side retry guidance in SDKs.

Artifacts / references:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RE/Probe+Filtering+and+Regional+Circuit+Breaker
- Prototype branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/tree/feat/probe-filtering
- Canary PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1432
- Fault-injection harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/reliability-tests/tree/main/probe-faults

Next steps / immediate tasks:
- Liam: land minimal probe-filtering kernel and add metrics -> PR #1432 (target by 2025-11-20).
- Maya: create canary plan and test matrix; coordinate with SRE for staging window.
- Sophie Martinez (SRE): provision canary environment and add alerting for probe_flip_rate and region_error_budget.
- QA: create load-shedding functional tests that validate priority routing and structured errors.

Notes: this ticket focuses on platform-level protections (probe filtering, circuit-breaker, shedding). Follow-on work will address per-model probes tuning, SDK backoff recommendations, and enterprise override UX in Console.
comments: 2025-11-13 Maya Patel: Initial design sketched with Liam. Decided to prioritize probe-filtering in the proxy to reduce blast radius and keep change scoped.
2025-11-16 Liam Chen: Prototype PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1432. Basic hysteresis + sticky readiness implemented. Needs tests and metrics.
2025-11-18 Sophie Martinez: SRE reviewed metrics plan. Requested additional counter for probe_debounce_backoffs and an alert when probe_flip_rate rate-of-change > 200%/5m.
2025-11-22 Ethan Park (PM): Confirmed customer impact scoring. Suggested adding a per-customer circuit-breaker opt-out for enterprise-managed Dedicated deployments.
2025-11-25 Liam Chen: Ran staging fault injection. Observed 68% reduction in probe flips under GC-like noise; scale_event_frequency down ~72%. P95 stable. Pushing changes to canary in us-west-2 next.

2025-11-30 QA: Load-shedding tests added to reliability-tests harness. Discovered that background batch jobs retried aggressively and caused burst retries; added jittered backoff to batch client library.

2025-12-03 Sophie Martinez: Approved runbook and alert thresholds. Recommend gradual rollout across regions with 6-hour observation windows.
